title: Weights, Axles & Overloading
whatItIs: Every lorry has legal limits for its gross weight, its train weight and each axle. Overloading is illegal: the vehicle is less stable, harder to steer and takes longer to stop.

keyFacts.text: A vehicle MUST NOT be used on a road if its weight, combination weight or any axle weight is over the legal maximum.

keyFacts: Gross vehicle weight includes the vehicle, load, driver and passengers. Train weight adds the trailer.
Use the Department for Transport plated weights: they're the legal limits in Great Britain.
Don't automatically trust declared weights or delivery notes: the responsibility is yours, not the customer's.

visual.caption: Maximum authorised weights: examples from the regulations

notes: *If conditions in the regulations are met. Axle spacing or your plate can set a lower limit.

a.label: Gross vehicle weight
points: Maximum permitted weight of the vehicle plus its load
Includes the driver and any passengers

b.label: Gross train weight
points: Maximum permitted weight of the vehicle plus any trailer
Also includes the weight of the trailer

onTheTest.question: You've made several drops and the rest of the load is at the front of the trailer. Why check your axle weights?
options: The gross weight is now higher
The new weight spread may overload an axle
Axle weights only matter when fully loaded
The train weight limit no longer applies
onTheTest.why: Removing part of the load reduces the gross weight, but the new weight distribution may overload individual axles.

onTheTest.question: Your vehicle has a manufacturer's plate and a Department for Transport plate. Which weights should you keep to?
options: Whichever plate shows the higher weight
The weight shown on the delivery note
onTheTest.why: Where a vehicle has both, the Department for Transport plated weights are the legal limits in England, Scotland and Wales.

traps: Gross train weight isn't gross vehicle weight: it includes the trailer being towed.
Lift or tag axle raised while loaded? Axle or gross weights could go over their limits.
Overloaded at a roadside check? Immediate prohibition, and the vehicle may be immobilised.
